summary: Allegany County steel CCC lookout built 1935 on Jersey Hill; staffed only as needed, removed August 1987; a fieldstone fireplace remains per the register.

facts.design: Steel fire lookout by the CCC; Starr list names it an Int. Derrick model 1933 tower
facts.status_note: Removed in August 1987; the register says only a fieldstone fireplace remains at the site

staffing.status: Staffed only on an as-needed basis by the Division of Lands and Forests

access.note: Site lies in Jersey Hill State Forest per the register; no source describes visitor access or a route to the spot

facts.agency: New York State Division of Lands and Forests; the register lists the NYSDEC as administrator of Jersey Hill State Forest

events.note: CCC built footers for a steel fire lookout tower
Erected by CCC workers in 1935; reported as 80 ft in a 1935 paper, 79 ft 6 in by Wikipedia and NYSFFLA
Spring 1935 press said an observer would soon be stationed and a cabin built for the observer
Ceased fire lookout operations as aerial detection grew
Declared surplus and removed in August 1987
Registered March 16, 2015; nominated by Kevin Daley

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 75 ft (register, 'about 75-feet'), 76 ft 9 in (Starr list), 79 ft 6 in (Wikipedia and NYSFFLA list) and 80 ft (1935 newspaper). No height_m recorded because the sources do not agree; the brief's 24.4 m matches the 80-ft newspaper figure.
The spring 1935 press said an observer would soon be stationed on the tower; Wikipedia later says it was staffed only as needed. The sources do not date the change, so the story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Brief status 'gone' confirmed. Heights disagree across five sources (75 to 80 ft), so no height_m is recorded; the story reports the spread. The access level is 'unknown': an earlier 'public' value was inferred from the state-forest location, and no source describes visitor access. Only the register describes what remains, and it is a single source. The brief's name 'Jersey Hill (West Almond)' is also called Birdsall Hill by the NYSFFLA list. A 2026 Allegany State Park fire-tower tour listing appeared in search but concerns a different, standing tower and is not used. No corrections to the brief.
